tools.title: Abandon stale rollout
tools.description: Releases the execution claim of one stale rollout job of an owned stack so that the stack can be retried with `retry-rollout`. Only a job that stopped reporting can be abandoned; any other job answers 409 `abandon_job_conflict` with the guard that refused. The body is empty and no command is sent to a server.

tools.title: Abort workload relocation
tools.description: Stops a relocation that has not finished and resumes the workloads on the source server, whose data was kept. The body must carry `owner_approved: true`. A relocation that already moved cannot be aborted (409), and an abort stays fenced until the nodes verify the state.

tools.title: Add one managed Node through native provider control
tools.description: Creates or resumes one deterministic Add-Server job for the exact owned StackKit deployment. The standard `Idempotency-Key` is mandatory. Replaying the same key with the same canonical request returns the original job, lease, runtime-server, resource-generation, and provider-operation correlations; reusing it with different intent fails with 409. The raw key is never persisted or returned. A lost response or an uncertain native-admission outcome remains resumable only with the same key. HTTP acceptance means native admission is durable and provider reconciliation is pending; it never claims that the VM is already provisioned or healthy. Fresh admission atomically reserves the authenticated tenant/owner capacity slot with the lease generation and provider operation. When authoritative native admission finds that bounded capacity full, it persists a non-retryable 403 outcome and replaying that denied job returns the same outcome. Exact replays of an already committed admission reuse its existing reservation. This version has no automatic reservation release: terminal or local decommission state alone does not free a slot. Lease inventory and feature-delivery flags never authorize or deny capacity. Hosted fresh admission also requires the v2-signed commercial runtime and provider entitlements plus the signed `cloud.runtime.credits` `managed_servers` mode/limit decision; feature flags alone never grant provider capacity. Self-host OSS uses its construction-fixed static release-manifest policy instead of a SaaS entitlement dependency.

A repeated action is a no-op, and a stale `If-Match` revision answers 412.

The token is stored encrypted and an existing attachment is never overwritten (409 `attachment_rejected`). Self-hosted installs only (503 otherwise).

No delegated maintenance origin is needed, since cancelling only withdraws work that has not reached the server. Cancellation and execution claim use the same queued-state compare-and-set. Repeating a successful cancellation returns its receipt; a claimed or finished job returns maintenance_not_cancellable. Cancelling never claims to stop a command that has already reached the server.

tools.title: Create action card
tools.description: Stores a card that describes one approved-action primitive, its target and its evidence sink for the authenticated owner. The card starts as `awaiting_grant` (no `grant` given) or `awaiting_approval` and runs nothing until it is approved and executed. An executor-bound primitive (`check-backup`, `run-backup`, `start-service`, `stop-service`, `restart-service`, `update-service`, `verify-stackkit-state`) takes its contract hash from the stack's pinned StackKits release. The caller names only its target scope and the input that selects the target (the `runtime-instance-ref` service key of a start, stop, restart or update); Homelab derives every target ref (server, StackKits node, current worker) and the derived inputs (an adopted application's exact container `application-ref`, the update's target release, the backup contract) from fresh inventory and refuses a supplied ref that differs. It requires the card's connector binding, which must carry the primitive's grant scope when the card executes; it carries no grant, waits in `awaiting_approval` and cannot be approved by a person: its one Gateway Decision is answered by the acting agent's equipment when it is executed. The body is decoded strictly and must stay under 64 KiB.

tools.title: Create a server install command

Homelab mints the one-time pairing token the command carries (15 minutes) and answers its id and expiry; the token is never an argument. With mode reinstall-guard it answers the Linux command for a server whose Guard update state is reinstall_required: run as root on that server, it installs the current Guard in place and keeps the enrollment and identity key unchanged. The token then only downloads the Guard and is never redeemed.

The kombify-cloud transport orders a billed managed server, the hypervisor transport creates a guest on the owner's hypervisor and connect-remote enrolls over SSH. The control plane accepts that confirmation only for a server it can prove offline (no heartbeat for longer than the stale window), without a lease and not operated by kombify or a provider: leased and provider-operated servers are proven absent by their provider. A confirmed server is never dispatched to; its agent credential is revoked and the server is retired. A server that reported recently is removed through its node.

For a managed target, a true ensure_rollout request dispatches the existing deploy pipeline only after proving that its selected active foundation lease and canonical Node equal this exact target. The API never reports the resulting job as already applied. The overlay is consumed only while deriving StackKits artifacts and this path never creates or selects a replacement VM.

An executor-bound card first files its one Gateway Decision, which the acting agent's equipment answers at once (an owner's Deny or standing exclusion refuses it), and is admitted against fresh inventory and the server's lifecycle authority (its VM lease, or the owner's own admitted server). `execution_id`, `trace_id` and `idempotency_key` bind one execution; repeating them returns the stored result. A card of operation class `drift-correction` also needs `compensation_card_id`, any other card must not send it. A missing approval or grant, an expired grant and a connector binding that does not match answer 403 or 409 with a stable `reason_code`.

tools.title: Execute an owned IONOS Managed App command
tools.description: Default-off hosted adapter. Requires a verified Edge tenant and subject, signed operation entitlement, and a fresh Cloud account allowance for provision, start, backup and restore. Cleanup requires an existing owned reservation and remains possible during Cloud outages or module rollback. Provision additionally requires the provision entitlement. Reserves an exact generation globally across placements before calling the worker. Stop and ambiguous outcomes retain the slot; release requires exact authoritative absence including isolation resources. Retry completed command IDs to replay receipts; synchronous execution is capped at four minutes and requires enough verified database identity lifetime. Reconcile uncertain dispatches with a new observe or decommission command. No tenant or provider input is accepted.

Homelab issues the own-application.lifecycle capability for this application, action, operation and review digest (at most 15 minutes); the node refuses any other. A tag update re-resolves the tag, checkpoints the data, verifies and rolls image and data back on failure. Requires Owner approval.

tools.title: Read available updates
tools.description: Per visible server: the operating-system update facts the Guard reports and every service with a newer version. A service whose `update_mode` is `stackkit_upgrade` is updated with the service `update` action (`run_managed_service_action`): the governed upgrade of its stack's StackKits release, which keeps a restore point, verifies the target live and automatically returns to the previous release when that verification fails. All managed services of one server share that release, so one `update` of any of them updates them all; get_job reads its `update_outcome`. `adopt_required` services must be adopted first. A service whose version was not compared is counted in `not_compared`, never reported as up to date. A StackKits-managed application also carries the verified application release feed facts: `application_update` (a security fix in every setting, else the newest checked version; the `update` action with `version` and `digest` moves only that application and get_job reads its `application_update_outcome`), `bundled` (arrives with a StackKits release), `advisories`, `security_fix`, and `not_verified` / `vulnerable` per server.

tools.title: Read backup health and failures
tools.description: Answers "why is my backup failing". Per visible server: the Guard-observed freshness of the newest snapshot (`state`, `reason_code`, `last_snapshot_at`), the restore drill, the stack's backup schedule and off-site store, the outcome per day, and the newest finished and the newest failed backup job with the step it stopped in and the error it recorded (`last_failure`). A fresh snapshot never proves a restore works; the restore drill says that. Nothing runs on the node to answer this read.

Registration expiry from RDAP and certificate expiry from the presented public TLS leaf are separate facts with independent sources and observation deadlines. Missing data stays unknown. Expected DNS is never inferred from observed addresses. Proxied origins are explicitly unobservable from recursive public DNS. tools.title: Read per-drive SMART and NVMe health evidence
tools.description: Authenticated, tenant-scoped projection of Guard drive observations. Self-hosted installations use their configured installation tenant. Hardware identities retain history independently of mutable device paths; replacements never inherit earlier readings. Anonymous observations have attempt-specific IDs and cannot establish historical continuity. Missing, unsupported, inaccessible, incomplete, stale and disconnected observations stay explicit and cannot imply healthy hardware. A server with no observations returns a missing state when selected explicitly. Last successful readings remain historical evidence when a new attempt fails. Only a complete inventory or an explicit missing observation can establish disconnection, and an unreadable identity at a seen path stays uncertain. Reads age evidence and condition episodes, without initiating collection, self-tests, repairs, provisioning or other device actions. Capacity growth forecasts remain on the separate storage-forecast route.

Each condition names its affected server and, when attributable, immutable drive identity, severity, observed evidence and recommended next step. Collection failures are distinct from hardware diagnoses. Stable episode IDs deduplicate unchanged conditions; resolved_at records recovery only when fresh evidence covers the condition. Anonymous collection incidents deduplicate by server and path, independently of anonymous hardware IDs. Nonzero cumulative counters describe historical totals; measured increases are separate conditions. NVMe command-error increases and consumed rated endurance are advisories, rather than standalone evidence of media failure. Resolved history is bounded to 64 episodes per condition scope and 90 days. Reads initiate no repair, device mutation or provider action.

Counts describe hourly sampled observations, not all ingested samples; sparse observations outside the backend lookback may be absent. No interpolation or per-service storage attribution is performed. Separate origin/source streams remain separate resources and are never summed. Guard OTLP times describe Guard collection, not original OTLP point time. pins.description: The owner's server choice per use case of an add-use-case change, use case id to server id. Every chosen server must belong to one deployment of the owner in this tenant, and every pinned use case must be part of `goals`.

planned_node.description: The node an add-server run brings, when its size is known before it enrolls.

tools.title: Recommend StackKits
tools.description: Computes ranked StackKit recommendations from the selected goals, the deployment lane and surface, and the authenticated owner's worker inventory and self-disclosure. Safe and idempotent: nothing is stored. A non-ready status (`incomplete`, `stale`, `degraded`) is still a useful answer that names the evidence to supply.

available_goals.description: Use cases the released catalog offers.

runtime_offering_id.description: Explicit planned provider offering; together with provider_id identifies its real package.

selection_intent.description: all asks which of available_goals the full-homelab template should preselect.

server_capacity.description: Advisory planning capacity, never attested rollout facts.

server_fit.description: Target server or managed offering for whole-stack fit evaluation.

tools.title: Recover the Guard session of a managed runtime
tools.description: Probes the canonical aggregate; when it cannot prove a Guard connection, restarts Guard over the pinned execution channel for an entitled owner of a running server and re-observes the connection within a bounded window, then converges enrollment to enrolled. A stopped runtime is refused (managed_runtime_stopped). No provider resource is touched.

tools.title: Record the outcome of an applied failure resolution
tools.description: Attributes a finished procedure job of the caller tenant to the failure resolution it applied and the failure signature it was applied to. The outcome is the job's terminal state (completed is succeeded, failed is failed), never a value the caller sends; a job that is still running or was canceled is refused. The context is the one of the tenant's own latest occurrence of that signature. The record stays in the tenant; repeating the call for the same resolution and job returns the stored record.

job_id.description: The tenant's job that ran the procedure.

procedure.description: Product procedure reference of the applied fix step.

resolution_id.description: Id of the failure resolution that was applied (find_similar_failures).

signature.description: Failure signature the resolution was applied to; the tenant must have an occurrence of it.

tools.title: Recreate one fully released managed server generation
tools.description: Explicitly provisions generation N+1 for the same provider-neutral runtime slot after generation N has terminal lease and canonical server state, terminal provider operation state, opaque provider-native absence evidence, and exact capacity release. The immutable provider, region, offering, role, StackKit, and service intent is recovered from the old owner-scoped lease; clients cannot replace it. The endpoint delegates to the same managed-runtime expansion authority as Add Node, so enrollment, Guard evidence, endpoints, and StackKit rollout proceed through the full Creation flow. A standard Idempotency-Key is mandatory and safely replays the accepted generation.

confirmed.description: Explicit acknowledgement that Recreate provisions and bills a new managed server generation.

tools.title: Reject layout recommendation
tools.description: Marks an open or snoozed layout recommendation of the authenticated owner as rejected so it is no longer offered, and answers its updated view. A recommendation in any other state answers 409 `layout_recommendation_changed`.

tools.title: Release an adopted lifecycle binding without deleting or stopping its runtime
tools.description: Release an adopted lifecycle binding without deleting or stopping its runtime

http_port.description: Stack it plan only: the container port the web UI listens on. Omitted keeps the detected port.

http_service.description: Stack it plan only, with adopt_compose_project true: the Compose service that serves the web UI.

memory_mib.description: Stack it plan only: memory limit of the rebuilt application in MiB. Omitted keeps the proposed limit.

no_outbound.description: Stack it plan only: block outbound network access of the rebuilt application.

own_application_name.description: Stack it plan only (mode stack_it): the own application name the container becomes. Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, starting with a letter, and not starting with kombify or stackkit. Omitted keeps the name derived from the container.

tools.title: Remove/deregister agent
tools.description: Remove/deregister agent

tools.title: Remove Cloud link
tools.description: Deletes the stored kombify Cloud profile link of the authenticated operator on this install. The link is per operator; nothing at kombify Cloud changes. When no link exists the call succeeds with `removed: false`. Re-linking is a browser sign-in and is not available to agents.

tools.title: Remove use case
tools.description: Retires an installed workload, or every installed workload of a catalog use case, through the native resolver against the baseline named by `expected_spec_hash`, and queues the StackKit lifecycle jobs. The workload stops running but its data is retained (`data_disposition: retain`). The `Idempotency-Key` makes a retry replay the original acceptance; refused with 409 while the stack is busy, a service is locked or a server is in maintenance.

expected_spec_hash.description: Native baseline hash read from the use-case configuration view.

selector_ref.description: Workload slug or catalog use-case id; no surrounding whitespace.

tools.title: Rename homelab
tools.description: Renames the authenticated owner's homelab. The homelab name is the Stack Identity name and syncs to kombify Cloud when connected. Reversible; the homelab is resolved from the authenticated owner, never from an argument.

tools.title: Rename server
tools.description: Writes servers.display_name, which runtime projections never overwrite. `null` or an empty string clears the rename. Requires the signed homelab.inventory.write entitlement and the FGA server `caller` relation; the write is bound to the authenticated tenant and owner, and a server outside that scope is denied without revealing whether it exists. The canonical inventory `name` reports the chosen name when one is set.

tools.title: Prepare the pairing command that re-pairs this server
tools.description: Issues a one-time install command for a server whose Guard pinned no binding signing key. The token is returned once. Mutating commands stay refused until the server is paired again.

tools.title: Repair drifted host security controls
tools.description: Requests a bounded repair of controls the fresh host security evidence reports as drifted and automatically repairable. Requires the server's owner, the Edge-signed `homelab.servers.maintenance` entitlement and, on the person's own session, a fresh multi-factor sign-in (at most 300 seconds old); an agent acting for the person needs no step-up. The repair travels as a typed, journaled Guard command that runs `stackkit host security repair --apply` for exactly the named controls; StackKits refuses, before changing anything, a change that would cut the management path or lock the owner out. Bounds: one repair per server at a time (409 `repair_in_progress`), a per-control cooldown (429 `repair_cooldown`), a daily attempt budget per control (429 `repair_attempts_exhausted`) and a circuit breaker after consecutive failures (429 `repair_circuit_open`); the 429 answers carry `retry_after`. A control that is compliant (409 `control_not_drifted`), under an approved exception (`control_has_exception`), manual (`control_not_repairable`), blocked on an authorized SSH key (`needs_authorized_key`) or not observed is refused. The body is decoded strictly.

tools.title: Repair one degraded component of a completed rollout on its existing server
tools.description: A rollout whose stack core applied completes degraded when an independent component could not finish; the component is recorded in the stack's `degraded_components` and repaired automatically. This operation starts that repair now. `public_tls` installs the managed kombify.me origin certificate (ADR-0047) on the stack's server; its hostnames come from the degraded rollout, never from the request. Answers 409 `component_repair_not_needed` when nothing is degraded.

tools.title: Request fresh service logs
tools.description: Asks the service's agent for its latest log lines, bound to a fresh inventory revision of the service's server. The node collects one bounded page into a durable read job; read the page with `GET` on the same path (`get_service_logs`) or follow `job_id` with `get_job`. It changes nothing and stays open on a frozen service. The service must advertise `logs` in `allowed_actions`. Exact replays under the same Idempotency-Key converge on the same job and a different body under the same key is 409; the raw Idempotency-Key is never persisted.

cursor.description: Opaque StackKits cursor from the prior page.

tools.title: Restart onboarding
tools.description: Clears the authenticated owner's completed and seen steps in a journey and reactivates it so the tour is shown again. Only the owner's own progress changes; no infrastructure is touched. Answers the resolved journey like the action route.

tools.title: Trigger drift resolution (re-apply)
tools.description: Precondition -- stack must have status "drifted"

tools.title: Release an unresolved Guard command outcome
tools.description: Commits an append-only operator resolution revision for an operation whose outcome is unknown and releases the worker's fence. `disposition` is `verified_applied` (the effect is in place), `verified_not_applied` (nothing happened) or `accept_unknown` (release without a verified outcome); `note` records what was verified. The actor is the authenticated subject and is recorded with the revision; a Guard cannot commit these dispositions. The person's own session needs a fresh multi-factor sign-in (at most 300 seconds old); an agent acting for the person needs none. `expected_revision` must be the revision the list returned, otherwise 409 `outcome_revision_stale`. The body is decoded strictly: exact keys, no unknown fields.

tools.title: Archive a legacy or unbound custody record after provider cleanup
tools.description: Removes a non-executable legacy or unbound lease from the active dashboard only after the owner confirms that its provider resource was already removed. This operation never contacts or deletes a provider resource and is rejected for Homelab provider-controlled generations.

tools.title: Restore or remove the original container a Stack it kept
tools.description: Mode restore_original (within the 7-day retention) removes the rebuilt own application, keeping its volume, and starts the original again. Mode release_original removes the stopped original; its data stays. Both require Owner approval.

adopt_compose_project.description: Stack it plan only: adopt the whole Compose project the container belongs to instead of the single container.

cpus.description: Stack it plan only: CPU limit of the rebuilt application in cores. Omitted keeps the proposed limit.

http_port.description: Stack it plan only: the container port the web UI listens on. Omitted keeps the detected port.

http_service.description: Stack it plan only, with adopt_compose_project true: the Compose service that serves the web UI.

memory_mib.description: Stack it plan only: memory limit of the rebuilt application in MiB. Omitted keeps the proposed limit.

no_outbound.description: Stack it plan only: block outbound network access of the rebuilt application.

own_application_name.description: Stack it plan only (mode stack_it): the own application name the container becomes. Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, starting with a letter, and not starting with kombify or stackkit. Omitted keeps the name derived from the container.

tools.title: Resolve workload relocation
tools.description: Re-reads the transfer proof from the source and destination nodes of one relocation and records the verified outcome (`moved` or `aborted`). It is used when a move stopped between transfer and verification. The body is empty. While the nodes cannot both prove the exact transfer the answer is 409 and the relocation stays fenced.

tools.title: Restore Home Assistant to a recovery instance
tools.description: Restores a completed retained backup into the isolated recovery binding that belongs to the instance and verifies the result; the running instance itself is not overwritten. Requires the restore grant and an owned recovery binding (403 `recovery_not_authorized` otherwise). `operation_id` is a stable identity. A pending operation answers 202.

tools.title: Retry remote SSH enrollment
tools.description: Re-runs the Guard enrollment over the SSH connection persisted for a connect-remote deployment without rerunning the StackKit rollout. The deployment must belong to the authenticated owner and use the connect-remote transport; the credential comes from the Wallet node access item already bound to it, or from `ssh_wallet_item_id` when the connection should be rebound first. A plaintext password is never accepted by this contract.

ssh_wallet_item_id.description: Wallet node access item to rebind the stack's persisted SSH connection to before the retry.

tools.title: Resume one overdue managed Node wait on its exact existing VM
tools.description: Authenticated, idempotent recovery for a persisted `waiting_enrollment`, `waiting_provider_provision`, or `waiting_canonical_guard` job whose `next_resume_at` has been overdue beyond the bounded grace period. The server validates the owned StackKit deployment, source job, wait reason, exact lease, active foundation role, and canonical Node as one operation. It atomically retires the exact source wait, creates or rehydrates one deterministic replacement deploy bound to the same lease and Node, and replays that job on later calls. Before handler entry, queue workers atomically acquire the durable `tenant/stack` compatibility execution claim; this serializes different jobs for the same StackKit deployment across Homelab replicas. The claim remains durable `running` until the handler exits, including during cancellation. This endpoint never invokes provider VM creation or selects a newer VM. A replacement found durable `running` after a crash remains fail-closed, is reported as the same job, and is never duplicated automatically; runtime-action reconciliation remains a separate operator concern.

job_id.description: Persisted source job currently projected as waiting_enrollment.

lease_id.description: Exact managed foundation lease already bound to the source job.

tools.title: Retry one failed StackKit deployment rollout on its exact existing managed VM
tools.description: Validates the owned failed deploy, its exact active foundation lease, and canonical Node in one server-side operation. The deterministic durable replacement bypasses provider VM creation, wins a durable `tenant/stack` compatibility execution claim before handler entry, and is replayed on repeated calls to this operation. The claim serializes different jobs for the same StackKit deployment across replicas and remains fail-closed as `running` after a process crash until operator reconciliation.

candidate_spec.description: Optional canonical StackSpec repairing missing route, access and data dependencies of already admitted modules. The pinned CLI validates it; revision CAS and candidate digest bind retries. Applied installations must use their existing change-set authority.

current_spec_hash.description: Normalized current node intent hash for an exact failed INIT whose immutable retry lineage proves a prior failed APPLY on this runtime. Required only for that partial INIT recovery; rejected on other paths. This is solely the CLI atomic CAS precondition, never authorization. Obtain through the pinned CLI resolve on the same current canonical node document. The durable receipt seals this value and lineage against changed replay.

lease_id.description: Exact active managed foundation lease bound to the failed job.

owner_approved.description: Required true when supplying a canonical initial-rollout repair candidate.

source_job_id.description: Exact failed deploy job used as immutable retry evidence.

tools.title: Review or apply owner-scoped test-residue cleanup
tools.description: Two-phase cleanup for control-plane projections only. A `dry_run` returns the exact authenticated-owner E2E/runtime-cloud candidates and a stable revision-bound digest. `apply` recomputes the plan and accepts only that exact digest. This route never decommissions a lease, calls a provider, destroys infrastructure, or enqueues lifecycle work.

digest.description: Required for apply; copied unchanged from the reviewed dry-run.

stack_id.description: Optional exact deployment scope used by E2E cleanup.

tools.title: Return Home Assistant migration
tools.description: Starts the return run for an owned migration that completed or failed and kept its source archive: archive the target, stop it, return the exclusive attachments and start and verify the original. The return run id is the migration run id with `:rollback`, so repeating the call resumes it. Answers 400 when the migration is not in a returnable state and 404 for a run the caller does not own.

tools.title: Change a managed service
tools.description: Derives stack, server, agent, kit and service authority from fresh canonical inventory. Every agent-executed mutation (`start`, `stop`, `restart`, `update`, `backup`, adopted applications included) runs as one governed RIL action card, its only write path: the card is derived from the service, its server and worker (an adopted application by its exact container, `update` with the pinned release, `backup` with the stack's backup contract), its one Gateway Decision is answered by the acting agent's equipment (no per-call approval flag), and the executor-bound primitive (`start-service`, `stop-service`, `restart-service`, `update-service` or `run-backup`) runs through the same lease, one-use claim, node proof, dispatcher and evidence as `/v1/ril/action-cards`. The response names the card in `action_card_id` and its execution in `job_id`; read it back with `get_action_card` for its status and evidence. `freeze` and `unfreeze` set the owner guardrail in the control plane without reaching the node. This operation only changes a service: a log page is requested with `POST /api/v1/registry/services/{serviceId}/logs` and read with `GET` on the same path. Exact replays converge on the same card receipt and a different body under the same key is 409; the raw Idempotency-Key is never persisted. A start or restart is followed by StackKits verify before measured state changes. Agent-executed actions refuse with 409 `maintenance_active` while the server is being rebooted or updated, a kit whose backups are managed refuses `backup` with 403 `managed_backup_custody`, and a locked service, application group or (for `update`) stack refuses on both entries.

body.description: Either an agent-executed runtime action bound to a fresh inventory revision, or an owner lock action executed entirely in the control plane. The lock is not bound to an inventory observation: an owner must be able to freeze a service whose agent is unreachable.

acknowledge_untested.description: Application update only; the owner accepts an unchecked release on their own responsibility.

action.description: `update` runs the StackKit upgrade of the owning stack to the pinned release; it is accepted only while `allowed_actions` advertises it, which a managed service does while its server's Guard runs an older StackKits release than the published one. The upgrade keeps a restore point, verifies the target live and automatically returns to the previous release when that verification fails; the card's evidence states which (`service-update-succeeded`, `service-update-returned-to-previous-release` with recovery `recovered`, or a failure code). For a StackKits-managed application whose version fact is `application_update`, `update` with `version` and `digest` moves only that application to that release: the node checkpoints its data, updates it and rolls it back automatically when generate, apply or verify fails. The job result's `application_update_outcome.result` is `updated`, `rolled_back`, `rollback_failed` or `refused` (with `reason_code`). The server re-checks a fresh fact: the version must be one of `newer_versions` with its exact digest and the same major version; an unchecked version needs `acknowledge_untested`; under `with_stackkits_releases` only a security fix (`advisory_id` of the fact's `security_fix`) is admitted. A refusal is 409 with `reason_code`. `backup` takes one out-of-band snapshot of the owning stack (Basement kits; managed kits keep their schedule).

advisory_id.description: Application update only; the high advisory the fact's `security_fix` closes.

digest.description: Application update only; the release's manifest digest from the fact.

version.description: Application update only; the release (image tag) from the fact's `newer_versions`.

oneOf.description: Asserts or clears the owner mutation lock. Applied synchronously by the control plane, so the response carries no job id and reports status `completed`. Repeating the same lock state is a no-op.

tools.title: Run full unifier pipeline (validate + analyze + unify + generate)
tools.description: Side-effecting -- generates IaC output files.

tools.title: Start, stop or restart an unmanaged container of an owned server
tools.description: Requires the Edge-signed `homelab.servers.maintenance` entitlement, ownership of the server in the tenant, the Inventory operate grant on the server and a connected, current Guard that advertises `stackkit.host-operate.v1`. The body is decoded strictly: exact lowercase keys `container` (a container name or id) and `action` (start, stop or restart), no duplicates, no unknown fields, no approval flag. The action is one governed RIL action card, its only write path: the primitive `start-host-container`, `stop-host-container` or `restart-host-container` binds exactly this verb and this container (`host-container-ref`) on the server's node, its one Gateway Decision is answered by the acting agent's equipment (D-2026-10-23-06), and it runs through the same lease, one-use claim, node proof, dispatcher and evidence as `/v1/ril/action-cards`. The server's stack must have an applied plan (409 `host_action_plan_unavailable`). The response names the card in `action_card_id` and its execution in `job_id`; read it back with `get_action_card`: the evidence carries the Guard's verdict. The Guard resolves the container to its full id, refuses a StackKits-managed container, one carrying any StackKits label (`container_managed`, use the managed service actions), a container that is removed when it stops (`container_autoremove`, that would be a deletion) and the platform's own agents (`container_protected`), acts on that id and reads the state again; an action that does not reach its target state fails with `state_not_reached`. Nothing is deleted: removing a container or its data is not an action. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key converges on the same card instead of running the action twice, and a different body under the same key is 409. There is no free-form shell path. Refusals are client-error-envelope/v1 documents; 409 `reason_code` is one of node_protected, agent_not_connected, heartbeat_stale, agent_capability_missing, container_protected, host_action_stack_unavailable or host_action_plan_unavailable at the route, or a governed-action reason (entitlement, a running stack mutation, maintenance, a stale target) when the card is created or begins. The Guard's own refusals and failures (container_managed, container_autoremove, container_not_found, engine_unavailable, precheck_failed, action_failed, state_not_reached, readback_failed) are the card's evidence summary codes `guard-refused-<code>` and `guard-failed-<code>` (code with hyphens). A host action no longer appears on the server timeline: the card is its record.

container.description: A container name or id from the container list.

tools.title: Queue an owned server OS update plan, OS update or reboot
tools.description: Requires the Edge-signed `homelab.servers.maintenance` entitlement, ownership of the server in the tenant, and current server-bound standing authority for delegated native MCP calls. These three ordinary actions require no fresh MFA or separate owner_approved assertion. Reboot and os_update require expected_impact_digest from the preview the user confirmed. Impact is compared atomically at admission and again at execution claim; changed or incomplete evidence sends no command and requires a refreshed preview and renewed confirmation with a new request key. The body is decoded strictly: exact lowercase keys, no duplicates, no unknown fields. A replay with the same Idempotency-Key returns the stored receipt before target validation. One reboot or OS update and, separately, one update plan may be active per server; a job not finished by its deadline fails with `deadline_exceeded` and frees its slot. The action is offered in `allowed_actions` only when the server agent advertises `stackkit.host-maintenance.v1`, and `reboot` only when the server also reports `host_boot_id`. Refusals are client-error-envelope/v1 documents; 409 `reason_code` is one of control_plane_host, substrate_node, protected_demo_server, service_locked, maintenance_active, node_operation_active, plan_stale, agent_capability_missing, boot_id_unknown, agent_not_connected, heartbeat_stale, inventory_revision_stale, idempotency_key_reused, impact_confirmation_required, impact_changed or impact_unavailable; 403 carries entitlement_required or maintenance_origin_authority_denied.

expected_impact_digest.description: Required for os_update and reboot, forbidden for os_update_plan. snapshot_digest of the current impact preview confirmed for this exact server and action. Changing it under an existing Idempotency-Key is a conflict; a renewed confirmation uses a new key.

expected_plan_digest.description: os_update only: the plan_digest of a completed os_update_plan for this server that is at most 15 minutes old.

owner_approved.description: Optional legacy field; it does not grant maintenance authority.

tools.title: Start, stop or restart a service unit of an owned server
tools.description: Same authorization and admission as the container action. The body takes the exact lowercase keys `unit` (one `.service` unit name), `action` (start, stop or restart), no approval flag. The action is the governed primitive `start-host-unit`, `stop-host-unit` or `restart-host-unit` (unit in `host-unit-ref`), the same card path as the container action. Units of the management path (the Guard, kombify and StackKits services, sshd, Docker, containerd, systemd itself, D-Bus, the network, firewall, VPN and clock stack and the like) are refused here and again by the Guard (`unit_protected`), also when an alias of the unit or a unit that requires it is protected; an unknown unit answers `unit_not_found` and a template instance that is not running `unit_instance_unknown`. The Guard reads the unit state after the action; the card's evidence carries its verdict. Retry and refusal behavior are those of the container action.

unit.description: One service unit name, for example the unit a process reports.

tools.title: Send command to agent
tools.description: Send command to agent

tools.title: Get server access context
tools.description: Returns address metadata, channel state, and freshness-qualified service links only. It never returns endpoint references, access-profile references, route IDs, credentials, tokens, SSH users, ports, keys, commands, or logs. This surface requires inventory operate permission; read permission alone is insufficient.

tools.title: Get server health
tools.description: Get freshness-qualified health for one owned server

tools.title: Get server ports
tools.description: Projects compiler-declared listener claims and generation-fenced reservations beside monotone Guard runtime evidence. Missing or stale observations remain explicit and never become optimistic availability.

tools.title: Set notification preferences
tools.description: Writes the topic-by-channel preference matrix of the authenticated user. Homelab forwards the body (at most 1 MiB) to the notifications engine unchanged; the engine rejects unknown topics and channels with 400 and silently ignores channels that are locked for a topic. The answer is the fresh matrix, not wrapped in the `data` envelope. Quiet hours and the Telegram link are read-only here.

only_if_unset.description: When true, a channel the user already set is left as it is.

channels.description: Channel name (email, in_app, slack, sms, push, telegram) to its new state.

tools.title: Set operator self-disclosure
tools.description: Replaces the signed-in operator's whole self-disclosure; an unanswered question means "not told". The body is decoded strictly and every answer must come from the closed vocabulary below. The capability profile in the answer is derived by the Unifier, never stored from the request. With `if_unchanged` the replacement is applied only when the stored value still equals it, otherwise the answer is 412 `self_disclosure_changed`.

if_unchanged.description: The stored value this replacement must still match.

source.description: link when the answers arrived as URL state and the operator confirmed them; homelab when typed in a Homelab surface.

tools.title: Confirm server availability
tools.description: The owner says whether the machine is on all the time (`always-on`) or switched off at times (`part-time`). The statement is stored next to what the Guard observed and replaces the observed class for planning. `unknown` or `null` withdraws it. Owner only; any other caller gets 404.

class.description: always-on or part-time confirms; unknown or null withdraws the confirmation.

tools.title: Publish a server service at its kombify.me address, or stop publishing it
tools.description: Nothing is published by default: a paired server has no public route and the relay carries no traffic. The owner enables it per server with an explicit `service` name and `target_port` (the origin is always the Guard host's loopback, never another machine) and may withdraw it at any time. The relay authenticates the Guard, not the visitor, so what answers on that port must protect itself. Enabling requires the owner, the `homelab.servers.maintenance` entitlement and, on the person's own session, a fresh multi-factor sign-in (reason `server_reach_step_up_required`); an agent acting for the person needs no step-up. Withdrawing is never gated. Responds with the reach section of the server read model; the reconciler then creates or withdraws the route.

service.description: Required when enabling. The route label; the kombify.me route is <base>-<service>-<server suffix>.

target_port.description: Required when enabling. The port the service listens on, on the Guard host's loopback (the host is fixed).

tools.title: Approve or withdraw automatic security repair
tools.description: Off by default. An approval names controls from the safe set (`allowed_controls`: brute-force protection, the firewall policy, kernel parameters and automatic security updates; never the ssh controls), expires within 90 days and never renews itself. While it is in force the control plane repairs a named control that fresh evidence reports drifted, inside the same bounds as an operator repair. Requires the owner, the `homelab.servers.maintenance` entitlement and, on the person's own session, a fresh multi-factor sign-in; an agent acting for the person needs no step-up. `enabled: false` withdraws the approval.

tools.title: Set a server's update setting
tools.description: Stores the server's update setting (`ask`, `automatic` or `with_stackkits_releases`) for the owner of the worker and records the change with its actor in the audit log. Reversible.

tools.title: Enable or disable a substrate binding
tools.description: Binds the substrate to the Guard's current authenticated inventory (node, guest-id range, image pins) and turns guest placement on or off. Optimistic concurrency: `revision` must equal the current binding revision (0 when none exists) and the answer carries the next one. Refused with 409 while the substrate has no current inventory, no node-local configuration, a revision mismatch, or non-decommissioned guests that still hold custody.

revision.description: Current binding revision; 0 creates the binding.

tools.title: Ensure or revoke one declared owned Home Assistant connector on its node
tools.description: Requires fresh backend ownership, positive operate authority, exact current inventory and Owner approval. Transports only closed correlation metadata through Guard to the published pinned CLI, whose local signedApply and Owner setup authority remain mandatory. Stores pre-send durable intent; unknown acknowledgement only reconciles the original operation read-only. Current v0.51.8 lacks the supporting catalog and returns nondispatchable SourcePreview. Credentials stay in node custody.

tools.title: Snooze layout recommendation
tools.description: Hides an open or snoozed layout recommendation of the authenticated owner until `until`, which must lie in the future and within 90 days, and answers its updated view. A recommendation in any other state answers 409 `layout_recommendation_changed`.

until.description: End of the snooze, at most 90 days ahead.

tools.title: Start Home Assistant migration
tools.description: Starts (or resumes) the durable migration run for an authorized local binding: archive the source, provision an isolated target on the owner's own substrate, restore and verify it, then wait for the cutover confirmation. The run id is derived from tenant, owner and target, so repeating the call resumes the same run. The request must match the binding's source service and authorization reference exactly (403 otherwise). Self-hosted installs with a configured local binding only (503 `migration_executor_unavailable` otherwise).

authorization_ref.description: Opaque reference of the binding's authorization; not a secret.

tools.title: Join a server to the homelab's identity Authority
tools.description: Joins this kit deployment's server to the server that runs the homelab's Pocket ID (the homelab's authority pointer, never a client choice). The job runs the pinned StackKits CLI on each server: the join request pinned to `authority_root` (the root fingerprint the Owner reads at the Authority's console or Hub), the Owner's passkey approval in the Authority's Hub (the job waits up to five minutes), the install of the Authority-signed trust bundle, the joined server's sign-in client registered at the Authority (a second passkey approval) with its secret delivered only through the homelab's Wallet, and the homelab DNS zone on every server. The server joins after its StackKit init and before its first apply; its own domain is always one of the hostnames. Homelab carries the documents and signs none of them. Needs exactly one Idempotency-Key; a replay returns the same job and never asks for approval again.

authority_root.description: SHA-256 fingerprint of the Authority's root as the Authority shows it; only a trust bundle under it installs.

hostnames.description: Further names the server serves inside the homelab domain; its own domain is always added.

tools.title: Start a stopped managed server of the same generation
tools.description: Admits one generation-bound provider-control reconcile toward running. The provider power-on runs once under an at-most-once claim; a repeated request while it converges replays the same operation. Requires the managed runtime entitlement before any provider call.

tools.title: Read, review or back up an own application adopted with Stack it
tools.description: Queues one StackKits own-application step for an application StackKits runs as an own application and Stack it adopted: status or logs (reads), backup (Owner approved, a node snapshot holding every own application volume), or the dry run of a mutation: review (start, stop, restart or rollback), update_review (a newer version tag of its own image, optionally allow_major), checkpoint_rollback_review or checkpoint_discard_review (the data checkpoint of a tag update). A dry run changes nothing and returns the review digest the execution binds.

allow_major.description: update_review only; admits another major version or an unversioned running image.

checkpoint.description: Checkpoint reviews only; the operation ID of the tag update that took it.

image_tag.description: update_review only; a newer version tag of the application's own image.

tools.title: Move workloads to another server
tools.description: Starts a verified move from the source server (this stack, `source_agent_id`) to a destination server of another owned stack. With `engine: native` it moves one installed `use_case` or one application (`workloads`): the destination adds it, receives the encrypted data straight from the source and reads its health and data back before the source is retired; the source stays stopped with its data until then and runs again when the move stops. With the Coolify engine (default) select either whole `projects` or individual `resource_uuids`; the transfer secret stays in Wallet custody (`wallet_item_id`) and domain switches go only to test domains. Needs exactly one Idempotency-Key; a replay returns the same job. Refused with 409 when a target holds locked services or server maintenance runs.

destination_agent_id.description: Guard agent of the destination server; must differ from the source.

items.description: OLD=NEW host names; NEW must be a test domain.

engine.description: native moves installed applications; coolify (default) moves Coolify projects or resources.

projects.description: Whole Coolify projects to move. Mutually exclusive with resource_uuids.

resource_uuids.description: Individual Coolify resources to move. Mutually exclusive with projects.

source_agent_id.description: Guard agent of the source server in this stack.

use_case.description: engine native: the installed use case to move with all its applications. Mutually exclusive with workloads.

wallet_item_id.description: Coolify engine only: Wallet item id (itm_...) of the transfer secret; never the secret itself.

workloads.description: engine native: one installed application (workload ref) to move. Mutually exclusive with use_case.

tools.title: Stop a managed server without destroying it
tools.description: Admits one generation-bound provider-control reconcile toward stopped. centron uses its graceful guest shutdown action; IONOS shuts the guest down over the execution channel because the IONOS provider stop releases the bound DHCP IPv4. The server keeps its disk, address, lease, capacity reservation and monthly billing.

tools.title: Sync stack identity with Cloud
tools.description: Takes the kombify Cloud stack identity record (read by the caller through the Gateway with the user's own token; `null` when Cloud has none) and applies the sync rules to the local copy: adopt the Cloud record, confirm an identical one, or answer the body to push to Cloud with the `If-Match` revision. The call itself never writes to Cloud. When no local stack identity exists yet it only reports `homelab_missing`.

cloud.description: The Cloud record, or null when Cloud has no stack identity.

tools.title: Test SSH to a discovered device
tools.description: Opens one SSH connection with the login held in the Wallet item `ssh_wallet_item_id` (its key when it holds one, otherwise its password; a built-in wallet item must name this IP as its URL), resolved inside Homelab and never answered; nothing is stored. This contract accepts no password. A failed connection answers 200 with `success: false`. Callers other than the owner of a self-hosted installation may only test IPs from their own discovery results; the owner may test arbitrary IPs. Local control planes only.

ssh_wallet_item_id.description: Wallet item holding the SSH key or password.

tools.title: Test remote SSH
tools.description: Opens one SSH connection to the given host with a credential held in the Wallet and reports whether it succeeded; nothing is stored. The credential is a Wallet node access item (`ssh_wallet_item_id`, bound to the host) or, on deployments that read the built-in wallet, the label of a stored SSH key. This contract accepts no password or private key. A failed connection answers 200 with `success: false` and the error.

ssh_key_label.description: Label of a stored SSH key; only on deployments that read the built-in wallet.

ssh_wallet_item_id.description: Wallet node access item holding the SSH key or password.

tools.title: Update Home Assistant
tools.description: Updates the instance to the exact `version`. It requires a completed backup (`backup_operation_id`) whose archive passed an isolated restore, the update grant on the binding and a pinned version (core `YYYY.M.P`, os `M.N` or `M.N.P`). `operation_id` is a stable identity and an uncertain submission is never repeated. A pending operation answers 202.

backup_operation_id.description: The verified backup taken before the update.

tools.title: Update stack identity if unchanged
tools.description: Revision-checked variant of the stack identity update. `If-Match` carries the `local_revision` read from the stack identity, in double quotes (for example `"3"`); a stale revision answers 412 and a reused `Idempotency-Key` with different content answers 409. The edit is stored locally and marked pending until it is synced with kombify Cloud. The body is limited to 4096 bytes. Requires the Postgres control plane (503 `stack_identity_store_unavailable` otherwise).

if_match.description: Strong local revision in double quotes, for example `"3"`.

tools.title: Update wallet item
tools.description: Merges the supplied fields into an item the caller owns and returns it redacted. Fields that are not supplied keep their value, including the stored secret and TOTP, which this contract can neither read nor change: the person sets those in the Wallet. The item kind and owner are immutable. An item owned by someone else answers 404. Only deployments that keep credentials in Homelab's own Wallet serve this route; elsewhere it answers 409 `self_hosted_only`.

notes.description: Free text; never put credentials here.
